If we think of the derivative as a rate of change, our intuition allows us to see that this rela- tionship is reasonable. If y = ƒ(u) changes half as fast as u and u = g(x) changes three times as fast as x, then we expect y to change 3>2 times as fast as x. The derivative of the composite function ƒ(g(x)) at x is the derivative of ƒ at g(x) times the derivative of g at x. This is known as the Chain Rule (Figure 3.26).
